# Transcribe Audio

- Route: `/tools/transcribe-audio`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `transcribe-audio`

## Summary

Turn an MP3, WAV, M4A or any recording into text, captions or JSON with AI speech recognition on our own GPU servers. (AI tools)

## Details

Interviews, lectures, voice memos and meeting recordings are far more useful as text: searchable, quotable, translatable. Media Manipulator transcribes audio with a Whisper model on a GPU server we operate, so your recording never leaves our infrastructure, and returns plain text, VTT or SRT captions, or a JSON transcript with word timestamps.
### What it does
- Transcribes MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC and other audio with Whisper.
- Outputs plain text, VTT, SRT or JSON with timestamps.
- Detects the language automatically across dozens of languages.
- Runs on our own GPU; no third-party AI provider.
### How to use it
1. Upload audio: Any common format.
2. Choose an output: Text, VTT, SRT or JSON.
3. Transcribe: Whisper runs on our GPU server.
4. Download: Open the transcript viewer or save the file.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ogg, opus, flac, alac, ac3, wma
- Output: txt, vtt, srt, json
- Counts as one AI job; failed jobs are not counted.
### Technical details
- Uses whisper-ctranslate2 with a large multilingual model; accuracy is best on clear speech with little background noise.
- Run the Remove background noise tool first on noisy recordings for a better transcript.
- Transcription counts as one AI job, from the daily AI allowance rather than the everyday one; a failed job is not counted.
### Use cases
- Interview notes: Get a text you can quote from.
- Lecture transcript: Study from the text, search for terms.
- Podcast captions: SRT or VTT for the video version.
- Voice memo to text: Turn thoughts into a document.
### FAQ
Q: Which languages are supported?
A: Whisper handles dozens of languages and detects the language automatically.
Q: How accurate is it?
A: Very good on clear speech. Background noise, crosstalk and heavy accents lower accuracy; denoise first if you can.
Q: Is my recording sent to OpenAI?
A: No. The model runs on our own GPU server.
Q: Can I get speaker labels?
A: Not yet. The JSON output has word-level timestamps you can segment by.
Q: Does this count against my allowance?
A: Yes, as one AI job on the AI allowance, which is separate from the everyday one. Failed jobs are not counted.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Use when someone wants the words from an audio recording as text: a podcast, interview, voice memo or lecture in MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG or FLAC. Output can be plain text, SRT, VTT or JSON with timestamps, and the language is detected automatically.
When to send them elsewhere: If the source is a video file use Transcribe Video (transcribe-video). If they want a short written overview rather than the full text use Summarize Audio (summarize-audio). To translate an existing caption file use Caption Translator (caption-translator).
Related tools: transcribe-video (transcribe speech from a video file); summarize-audio (summary and chapters instead of a full transcript); srt-generator (subtitle file focused output); caption-translator (translate the resulting captions); remove-background-noise (clean a noisy recording first)
